For interferometric applications, the moderate baseline at this frequency simplifies platform implementation. Enhanced Sensitivity to Small-Scale Features: Ka-band is particularly responsive to fine surface structures such as snow grain size, roughness variations, and small water bodies. SWOT utilizes Ka-band radar interferometry to provide global measurements of water surface height. Similarly, the Sentinel-3 Next Generation Topography (S3NG-T) mission addresses comparable objectives, contributing to the Copernicus Altimetry Constellation, which provides fundamental measurement data for Earth observation. The high-power source plays a crucial role in Ka-band SAR and swath altimetry systems, as it directly influences overall system performance. Due to the high frequency of the Ka-band (approximately 35.75 GHz), efficiently amplifying RF power presents a significant challenge. In conventional high-power amplifiers (HPAs), especially helix-based traveling wave tubes (TWTs), component dimensions are becoming increasingly small, leading to complexities in manufacturing, assembly, and thermal management. The objective of this activity is design new TWT topologies for space HPAs at Ka-band, capable to handle high average power (beyond 160 W) and a peak power higher than 2000W BOL.
